disclaimer: This tool only helps you review your finances. Results are for reference — they are not an official Wealify conclusion and do not replace your own checks. If you see a transaction you do not recognise, contact support right away — in the US the dispute window is 60 days from the date the bank issued the statement.
deadline.active: Dispute deadline: {deadline} — {days_left} days left (60 days from the statement date {statement_date}).
deadline.expired: The dispute deadline {deadline} passed {days_over} days ago (60 days from the statement date {statement_date}). It is still worth asking Wealify support what options remain.
email_reason.sender_domain_not_registere: the sender name says {brand} but the domain does not belong to {brand}
email_reason.lookalike_domain: the domain is a near copy of the real one (a few characters differ)
email_reason.reply_to_domain_differs: the reply-to address uses a different domain than the sender
email_reason.unrecognised_sender_domain: the sender domain is not on the known list
email_reason.no_transaction_matches_the_: no transaction matches the amount in the email
email_reason.pressure_language: pressuring wording (asking you to act within a short deadline)
finding.recurring_subscription.title: Recurring plan: {merchant}
finding.recurring_subscription.detail: {merchant} charges {amount} {cadence}, {charge_count} times since {first_charge}. The next charge is expected on {next_charge}. Kept as is, that is about {annual_cost} per year.
finding.recurring_subscription.next_step: If you still use it, nothing to do. To stop it, cancel it yourself in the {merchant} app — I can only guide you, I cannot cancel anything.
finding.forgotten_subscription.title: You may have forgotten to cancel: {merchant}
finding.forgotten_subscription.detail: {merchant} still charges {amount} per cycle, but the last {charges_without_receipt} charges (since {since}) have no receipt email anywhere in the mailbox — {wasted_if_unused} in total for those cycles. The next charge is {next_charge}.
finding.forgotten_subscription.next_step: Please confirm yourself whether you still use {merchant}. If not, cancel it on their site — I can draft the cancellation steps for you to follow.
finding.price_increase.title: Silent price increase: {merchant}
finding.price_increase.detail: {merchant} went from {old_amount} to {new_amount} ({percent}%) starting {effective_on}. Kept as is, that is {annual_delta} more per year.
finding.price_increase.notice_found: A price-change email from {merchant} itself matches both amounts.
finding.price_increase.notice_missing: No price-change notice was found in the mailbox.
finding.price_increase.next_step: It is your call whether to keep or change the plan. I do not change or cancel plans.
finding.duplicate_charge.title: Possible double charge: {descriptor} {amount}
finding.duplicate_charge.detail: Two identical charges at {descriptor}, {amount} each, {seconds_apart} seconds apart on {occurred_on} ({first_time} and {second_time}).
finding.duplicate_charge.next_step: Check yourself whether you really paid twice. If not, contact Wealify support to open a dispute — I cannot open one for you.
finding.double_fee.title: Fee charged twice: {descriptor}
finding.double_fee.detail: {descriptor} was charged {count} times on {occurred_on}, {amount} each, {total} in total. That is {amount_extra} above a single charge.
finding.double_fee.next_step: Compare it with the fee schedule yourself and ask Wealify support if it should only apply once.
finding.duplicate_payin.title: Duplicate deposit: {amount}
finding.duplicate_payin.detail: On {occurred_on} the account received {amount} {count} times from {counterparty}, {total_credited} in total — same amount, same day, same sender.
finding.duplicate_payin.wallet.detail: The Wealify wallet was credited {amount} {count} times ({counterparty}), {hours_apart} hours apart ({first_time} and {last_time}), {total_credited} in total. Two entries for the same amount — whether that is two real credits or one booked twice is not something this data settles.
finding.duplicate_payin.next_step: Check with the sender and your notification emails. If only one transfer was real, ask Wealify support before spending it.
finding.transfer_not_on_card.title: Money left the account but has not appeared on the card: {amount}
finding.transfer_not_on_card.detail: On {occurred_on}, {amount} left the account to fund the card, but the card statement has no matching load within {searched_window_days} days. Gap of {amount}, cause not determined.
finding.transfer_not_on_card.next_step: Check the card balance in the app yourself. If it is still missing, contact Wealify support and quote the transaction reference listed under Sources.
finding.wallet_balance_mismatch.title: Wallet balance does not match: {gap} off
finding.wallet_balance_mismatch.detail: Adding up the wallet ledger ({event_count} entries) gives {computed}, but the wallet reports {reported} as of {reported_at}. Gap of {gap}, cause not determined.
finding.wallet_balance_mismatch.next_ste: Check the wallet balance in the app yourself. If it is still off, ask Wealify support — I only read the numbers, I cannot adjust them.
finding.unknown_merchant.title: Merchant could not be identified: {descriptor}
finding.unknown_merchant.detail: The statement shows “{descriptor}”, {amount} on {occurred_on} ({charge_count} charges, {total} in total). I could not identify the seller and I will not guess a name.
finding.unknown_merchant.processor_line: This charge was routed through the {processor} payment processor, so the statement shows the processor rather than the seller.
finding.unknown_merchant.next_step: Try to recall what you bought that day, or search the mailbox for {amount}. If you do not recognise it, contact Wealify support.
finding.missing_email.title: No email found for a {amount} charge
finding.missing_email.detail: {descriptor} — {amount} on {occurred_on}. The whole mailbox was searched and no receipt or confirmation matches it. The review threshold is {threshold} (the 90th percentile of your own spending).
finding.missing_email.next_step: Confirm yourself whether you made this purchase. If you do not recognise it, contact Wealify support promptly — the dispute window runs from the statement date.
finding.suspicious_email.title: Email appears to impersonate {claimed_brand}
finding.suspicious_email.detail: An email dated {received_on} from “{from_name}” <{from_addr}> refers to {amount}. Signals: {reasons}.
finding.suspicious_email.next_step: Do not click links or enter card details from that email. Open the official {claimed_brand} app yourself to check. I will not reply to this email on your behalf.
merchant.apple_bill: Apple's combined billing line: iCloud+, App Store or in-app subscriptions.
merchant.chegg: Online study service that renews automatically each month.
merchant.tmobile: US mobile carrier, collected by ACH debit.
merchant.square_prefix: The “SQ *” prefix means the shop collects payment through Square.
merchant.wholefoods: Grocery chain (owned by Amazon); the descriptor is shortened to WHOLEFDS.
merchant.doordash: Food delivery app; the name after the * is the restaurant.
merchant.mta: New York subway / bus fare, usually $2.75 per ride.
merchant.amazon: Amazon Marketplace; the code after US* is an internal order reference.
merchant.wire_fee: Per-order fee for an international or interbank wire.
refusal.cancel_subscription: I cannot cancel a plan for you — this tool only reads data, it never acts on your money or services. What I can do: list your recurring plans, point out the ones worth reviewing, and draft the cancellation steps for you to follow.
refusal.dispute: I cannot open a dispute or request a refund. I can only assemble the evidence (transaction references, dates, matching emails) and the 60-day deadline so you can contact Wealify support yourself.
refusal.money_move: I cannot transfer, withdraw or refund money — my access is read-only. I can help you review the cash flow so you can decide.
refusal.card_lock: I cannot lock or unlock a card. You do that in the Wealify app or by calling support; I can show you where and gather the transaction details you will need.
refusal.third_party_email: I do not email merchants, banks or any third party. I only prepare a draft for you to send yourself, and I only send reports to your own address after you confirm.
refusal.reassurance: I cannot conclude that your account is safe or unsafe — this data is not enough to say. What I can say is that {needs_confirmation} items need your confirmation and {insufficient_data} items lack enough data. Please review each one and decide yourself.
refusal.suffix: Would you like me to do the part I am allowed to do?
mail.confirm_prompt: The draft is ready. I can only send it to your own address: {owner_email}. Do you confirm sending it?
mail.owner_only: I am only allowed to send to your own address ({owner_email}). Any other address is refused.
cancel_guide.title: Steps for you to cancel {merchant}
cancel_guide.body:
1. Open the official {merchant} site or app and sign in.
2. Go to Account → Subscription / Billing.
3. Choose to cancel the renewal and keep the confirmation email.
4. After the next cycle ({next_charge}), check the statement again to be sure the charge stopped.
Note: I do not perform any of these steps for you.
fx.note: The statement is denominated in USD. Any ₫ figure is a reference conversion at the rate you configured ({rate} ₫/$ via NEXA_USD_VND_RATE), not a bank rate.
smalltalk.greeting: Hello. I'm Nexa, your statement review assistant. What would you like to look at — an overview, the items needing your confirmation, subscriptions, or a specific transaction?
smalltalk.thanks: You're welcome. Tell me if you want anything else checked.
smalltalk.farewell: Take care. Come back whenever you want the statement reviewed again.
smalltalk.identity: I'm Nexa, a read-only review assistant for your Wealify statement. I reconcile the account, the card and your email receipts, and flag duplicates, double fees, subscriptions and anything that needs your confirmation. I cannot move money, cancel a plan or open a dispute — the decision is always yours.
